I will soon start working on a TM language that will take a underlying TM as its model. The ideal TM for this is a multi tape TM with one input tape (which I will make read only), a constant number kkk work tapes, and an output tape. This has the clearest and easiest definition of space complexity.

Among the TMs in Mathlib and @Bolton Bailey ‘s PR, which one is the best option?

I'm currently working on something like this in my fork of cslib - I'm building on top of https://github.com/leanprover/cslib/pull/384 and I fully agree on the tape kinds. Would be great if we could do this together!
I started with an abstraction of the tapes as comma-separated binary (dyadic) numbers and got quite far with it:
https://github.com/crei/cslib/pull/1/changes#diff-0633b0efeb384a6d904e8caff738dc054c62773fa19eeb50d6aba6d6c3512787R25 - this is a machine that "negates" the left-most word on the tape and the proof for its semantics is just "simp; grind", which is super nice.
I realized that this abstraction is too limited, especially for log-space machines that have to navigate inside the input without the ability to copy it somewhere. Because of that I started to build a more flexible abstraction that should be able to model most inductive data structures: Every tape is the encoding of Data which is either a natural number or a list of Data. The current position of the tape head is modeled by a list of natural numbers, the branches taken when descending into the tree structure. With this abstraction, a TM to verify a SAT witness could be neatly given as follows: https://github.com/crei/cslib/pull/18/changes#diff-e1eb7baf431c6f2aff7927e19226bcc009d0c9bc6c50edca9ff286f3745431eeR89
I don't have the required simp lemmas for the list operations yet, but I hope that the semantics of the sat algorithm is also just proven by simp; grind.
Oh I just realized we already talked about this over at #Is there code for X? > Complexity theory

Yeah my PR added just single-tape TMs so it won't have this, but I hope with cslib#384 we can get something defined very similarly but for the tape structure you describe. Maybe there's a technical point about which tapes are input and output, obviously for 1-tape tms its the same tape, I guess there could be many permutations over which are read-only or write-only, I haven't thought deeply about how to handle that the best.
So I started working on single tape TMs. I think I want to define my own cost function first
I am trying to get both TMs and RAMs on top of cslib#372 this week
@Bolton Bailey one thing I am missing in your definition of BiTapes is the notion of an index in the tape i.e. tape position
Concretely I would like to be able to say things like "insert cell i into data structure if cell i was blank before and written to now"

Here is an early stage PR : https://github.com/leanprover/cslib/pull/415 a
Replaced by cslib#416

@Bolton Bailey : Question about your definition of space complexity. In complexity theory we traditionally distinguish between space used vs "extra" space used. That is, space used in addition to input and output space. Your model currently seems to take the total size of the tape at any given point. This is how you get log space classes like L or NL. How would you suggest doing this in SingleTapeTM? is my costing approach correct in your opinion?

I used the total size in the PR because it seemed like the most natural way of getting information about the length of the output, which is what I needed. But indeed, I have heard it is conventional to make "space" mean "extra space", so I think defining a cost model that does it that way is fine. It seems slightly simpler conceptually to define things with total space, and maybe easier to formalize theorems with, but conventions are conventions for a reason and making too many definitions without extra space might make it hard to link things up to Log-space machines later, so I am ambivalent.
Okay. Another thing. I am trying to compose TMs and rapidly reaching the conclusion that we should operate directly on the tape.
Progs can hold their internal states as variables. Actually there’s another option : evaluate a prog to a tm instead of running it.

In some ways, I have made design choices with single tape TMs to make composition easier - I required that the halting tape state of the TM must be the same as the initial tape state, so that I can switch directly to the computation of the next machine. It seems a bit trickier to have the input and output tapes be different. I guess you could run the first TM, define a different collection of states to write the output back to the input (except that you've said this is read-only, not sure what to do about that).

I am a bit confused about how to evaluate a Prog to a TM. How do we get the set of states of the TM from the Prog?
In that case prog would be a single step of a transition function. But I think I prefer the idea I started with.
I have made TM composition easier by changing the TM to an implicit parameter of the query
